Question Choices: Find the sum of the first 5 composite numbers.
Hints: Start at 2. A prime has exactly 2 positive factors; a composite has more than 2. One is neither. List in order before adding.
Solution: One is neither prime nor composite. Starting at 2, the first 5 composite numbers are 4,6,8,9,10. Add: 4 + 6 + 8 + 9 + 10 = 37.

Question Choices: What is the smallest composite number that is greater than 30 and not divisible by 2?
Hints: Test all required conditions together; start with multiples or odd numbers to narrow the search.
Solution: Only odd candidates need testing. 31 is prime; 33 is composite. The smallest qualifying number is 33. It has factors 1,3,11,33.

Question Choices: Select. There is a Class of 41 students. Can they make at least two equal groups, each with more than one student?: ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Equal groups with at least 2 groups and at least 2 in each require a factor pair with both factors greater than 1.
Solution: The only positive factor pair of 41 is 1 x 41. This would give one group or one student per group. Neither meets both restrictions, so No.
